terms.name: n
terms.meaning: one BIU command per element (CAModel white box: biu_send_count=n)

terms.name: B36
terms.meaning: under-filled 64B block fetches in the burst-short regime ([C*eb<32] x L@64B)

terms.name: P128
terms.meaning: same-128B-line collision pairs sum(cnt*(cnt-1)) over the 2-D address set

terms.name: S1024
terms.meaning: row x block incidences minus distinct blocks at 1KB grain (share = Lrow-L)

terms.name: D128
terms.meaning: 128B lines touched by >=2 rows, x[C*eb<32] (fitted coefficient is NEGATIVE: the same-fetch deduction)

terms.name: C
terms.meaning: explicit column count: per-row teeth (row-burst overhead / lane utilisation)

terms.name: BR
terms.meaning: row bursts issued in the burst-short regime ([C*eb<32] x R)

derived: addr(i,j) = i*OS + j*ISB  (bytes, base offset 0 / aligned buffer); R rows x C elements
L@B    = number of distinct B-byte blocks touched by the 2-D address set
Lrow@B = sum over rows of the number of B-byte blocks that row touches
share@B= Lrow@B - L@B   (blocks fetched once but touched by several rows)
multi@B= number of B-byte blocks touched by >= 2 different rows
pairs@B= sum over blocks of cnt*(cnt-1)  (same-block element collision pairs; = n-L when cnt=2)
w@B    = max over blocks of the element count (worst crowding)
burst_short = 1 if C*eb < 32 else 0   (MTE minimum burst is 32 B)
block-size scan: burst-short line penalty best at B=64 (15.81%) -> 32 (15.87) -> 128 (17.02) -> 256 (18.89); collision-pair term best at B=128 (15.81%) -> 64 (15.84) -> 32 (16.49) -> 256 (16.81)
simd_load_gather_r2.greedy_reference: greedy union-pool (624 keys, unconstrained WLS, w=1/T) saturates at k=47 -> 13.57% in-sample, but its 5-fold CV (same term list refit per fold) is 17.57%; parent-reported 73-term greedy = 11.08% could not be reproduced on this exact 678-pt set (my reproductions: 614-key v11 pool k=35 -> 16.12%, same pool with R=1 kept (750 pt) k=53 -> 14.09%)
simd_load_gather_r2.notes: 2-D gather is the SAME one-BIU-command-per-element machine as gather_r1 (CAModel: biu_send_count = n), but the 256B crowding computed on the 1-D stride pattern is the WRONG block set for a comb tile: corr(w@256B, T) = 0.121 and corr(w@128B, T) = 0.149, and a 1+n model is 45.4%.  Two mechanisms dominate instead. (1) A REGIME SWITCH at C*eb = 32 B - the MTE minimum burst.  When the payload of one row is narrower than a single minimum burst the tile cannot be walked as row bursts, and each block fetch plus each row burst is paid separately: [C*eb<32]*L@64B (+40.6 ns per 64B block) and [C*eb<32]*R (+25.1 ns per row burst).  This one indicator takes 1+n from 45.4% to 21.1%; it is the same threshold the repo already recorded as 'SIMD 2-4x slower when C*eb < 32' (fit_v11_stepwise comment). (2) SAME-BLOCK CROWDING of the 2-D address set, but at 128 B rather than 256 B: pairs@128B = sum over blocks of cnt*(cnt-1) (elements colliding inside one 128B line), +0.0844 ns per colliding pair. The DEDUCTION asked for is real and measurable: when several rows land in the same 128B line the line is fetched once for all of them, so the model credits -71.6 * [C*eb<32] * multi@128B (multi = 128B lines touched by >= 2 rows); that single term is worth 0.93 MAPE points (15.81 -> 14.88).  In the equivalent parameterisation 49.9*[C*eb<32]*Lrow@64B - 77.0*[C*eb<32]*share@64B the credit (77.0) is 1.55x the price of one row-line incidence (49.9), i.e. sharing across rows is worth more than one full duplicate fetch.  By contrast share@1KB has a POSITIVE coefficient: rows that share a 1KB block are rows whose pitch is small - a comb with dense teeth - and that costs extra. Residuals are flat across dtype (11.4-15.1%), C (11.0-15.2%), regime (13.1/13.3%) and campaign (12.3/14.7%).  The data is intrinsically noisy: target_spread up to 1.51 and the two 2-D campaigns (v1_2d/v3_2d) differ by up to 2.6x on repeated configurations. COMPARISON WITH GREEDY: this 8-term physical form (13.18% in-sample, 13.46% 5-fold CV) beats a fully data-driven greedy over a 624-key pool, which saturates at k=47 -> 13.57% in-sample and 17.57% in CV (i.e. the physics generalises, the greedy overfits). greedy union-pool (624 keys, unconstrained WLS, w=1/T) saturates at k=47 -> 13.57% in-sample, but its 5-fold CV (same term list refit per fold) is 17.57%; parent-reported 73-term greedy = 11.08% could not be reproduced on this exact 678-pt set (my reproductions: 614-key v11 pool k=35 -> 16.12%, same pool with R=1 kept (750 pt) k=53 -> 14.09%)
